Customer to provide list of in-scope subdomains and data residency constraints
action_items: Maya Chen: upload SOC 2 Type II PDF + short system narrative to shared folder (due: 2026-11-05)
Oliver Bates: prepare KMS integration runbook (HSM and cloud KMS variations) and example terraform snippets (due: 2026-11-09)

summary: Introductory posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO mapping, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO expectations, audit log retention, and KMS envelope flow. Redwood clarified hosted vs dedicated controls, read-only Trust Center access, and options for customer-managed keys. Customer asked for concrete artifacts and a follow-up ops session to validate KMS flow and data residency constraints.
topics: SOC 2 Type II evidence and system narrative
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. We're going to run through Aurora — sorry, Auriga's security posture alignment with Redwood's control catalog. I'm Maya, I'm the AE. Oliver's going to do the technical lift.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Thanks Maya. Quick ask up front, we want to understand exactly what evidence you provide for SOC 2 and ISO mapping, and also how KMS will actually look in the flow, because our auditors ask for the envelope flow diagrams.
[00:32] Oliver Bates: Yep, totally. We'll cover the Type II artifacts we typically share, the system narrative, and then walk through the KMS envelope flow. One note, Redwood supports hosted API with BYOK options for Dedicated and Private deployments, so you'll get different controls depending on which path you pick.
[00:48] Carlos Mendes: Quick clarifying question, when you say BYOK, do you mean customer-managed CMKs in, like, AWS KMS and an HSM option? Or is there a Redwood-managed HSM?
[00:57] Oliver Bates: Both. For hosted we have a Redwood-managed key by default, but you can bring your own CMK in the Dedicated/Private setup. We also support HSM integrations for on-prem HSMs, and we can show the wrapper/envelope pattern — stage encrypt with CMK, and we keep per-request ephemeral keys for session encryption.
[01:18] Lina Park: Do you log key usage events to the audit trail? Our policy requires key usage logging for at least one year.
[01:26] Maya Chen: Good point. We capture KMS events in audit logs; retention depends on the plan but we can export logs to your logging endpoint or S3. We'll document retention SLAs in the Trust Center.
[01:40] Priya Rao: Can you share the Trust Center link? We want read-only access to see configuration artifacts.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll grant a read-only view. I'll add that as an action item. The Trust Center includes SOC 2 evidence index, runbooks, and per-region deployment notes.
[01:58] Carlos Mendes: On RBAC and SSO — we use Okta with SCIM for provisioning. How granular is Redwood's role model? We need ability to map to our least-privilege roles: auditor, operator, developer.
[02:12] Oliver Bates: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Roles are pluggable — we have built-in roles and you can create custom roles with scoped permissions. There are some edge cases where the 'admin' role controls both billing and key material access; you can split those in your Dedicated deployment.
[02:31] Priya Rao: Is there an option to separate billing from key management so that finance doesn't have access to KMS material?
[02:38] Maya Chen: Absolutely, that's a common ask. In Dedicated/Private we can gate KMS operations behind a separate role and we can integrate with your IAM for key access control.
[02:46] Oliver Bates: I'll note though that in Hosted we have separation internally, but billing access is consolidated for the portal. If you need strict separation we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[03:02] Priya Rao: OK. About reports — what's in the SOC 2 packet?
[03:07] Maya Chen: We provide the SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer-sensitive data, the system narrative, control mapping spreadsheets that map our controls to common frameworks like NIST/ISO, and sample evidence or evidence indexes. For ISO 27001, we provide mapping and the Statement of Applicability summary.
[03:25] Lina Park: Do you include network diagrams? Our auditors want diagrams showing VPC peering, subnets, and where logs are exported.
[03:33] Oliver Bates: We can provide an architecture diagram at a level that's suitable for auditors — not cloud account specific but shows region, VPC equivalents (we sometimes say V-PC in transcribed notes), network isolation, and data flow. For Dedicated/Private we can provide customer-specific diagrams.
[03:50] Carlos Mendes: About audit logs — if we need a copy for our SIEM, how does the export work? Is it push or pull? And what's the retention?
[03:59] Oliver Bates: Logs can be exported via push to your logging endpoint (e.g., Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or S3) or you can pull via our logging API. Retention: default hosted retention is 90 days, Dedicated can be configured for longer retention, and we can do archival exports to your bucket for 1+ year depending on contract.
[04:22] Priya Rao: Data residency — we have EU and APAC customers. Can you guarantee no cross-border movement for EU tenant data?
[04:30] Maya Chen: We support region pinning for data residency; for strict regulatory needs we recommend a Private deployment in region or Dedicated capacity pinned to a region. We also offer egress controls and routing policies.
[04:45] Priya Rao: We need to see proof points on that — previous SOC 2 attestations that the region pinning worked in audits.
[04:52] Maya Chen: We'll include regional deployment notes and attestations in the Trust Center evidence index.
[05:00] Carlos Mendes: On encryption again — if we do BYOK, where are the KEKs stored? Are they in our account?
[05:08] Oliver Bates: For Dedicated with BYOK we can either have the CMK in your cloud account (recommended) or brokered by a third-party HSM. The envelope keys used by the runtime are ephemeral and not retained beyond the request life.
[05:21] Lina Park: Does Redwood ever have access to plaintext?
[05:24] Oliver Bates: Operationally, service engineers can access sanitized logs for debugging but plaintext is not stored persistently. For highly-sensitive use cases we recommend Private on-prem or bring-your-own-key in your account so you control the root of trust.
[05:40] Priya Rao: About control mapping — can you show a sample row in the control mapping spreadsheet that ties an infra control to SOC 2 CC6 or ISO A.10?
[05:49] Maya Chen: Yep, the mapping spreadsheet maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 CCs and ISO clauses. We'll share a sample mapping row in the packet.
[05:58] Carlos Mendes: Any blockers we should plan for during procurement? We have legal who will push for a DPA and some custom SLAs on log retention and data deletion timelines.
[06:07] Maya Chen: DPAs are standard. For custom SLAs we'll engage solutions and legal; we can provide draft language.
[06:14] Priya Rao: Can you run a quick sketch of the KMS envelope flow? I know you mentioned it but auditors like diagrams.
[06:20] Oliver Bates: Sure, rough flow: client request -> application encrypts payload with ephemeral data key -> data key encrypted with CMK (in your account if BYOK) -> encrypted blob sent to Redwood -> runtime holds encrypted blob and uses ephemeral session keys for in-memory decryption only during processing -> results re-encrypted and returned. Key usage logged to KMS audit.
[06:44] Priya Rao: When you say "session keys" are those retained anywhere?
[06:47] Oliver Bates: No, ephemeral session keys are in-memory only and destroyed after request completion. We do capture high-level operational telemetry but not full plaintext.
[06:56] Carlos Mendes: What about cache — KV cache, is any plaintext cached on disk?
[07:00] Oliver Bates: KV cache is in-memory with encrypted backups where applicable; persistent caches are encrypted and keys managed per the deployment profile. Sometimes transcript or transcript tool shows KV as "KV cash" but it's cache.
[07:12] Maya Chen: Sorry yes, that was a transcript thing.
[07:15] Priya Rao: Our auditors will want to see your change control evidence for config changes. Is that in the evidence index?
[07:22] Oliver Bates: We include change control logs, release notes, and deployment audit trails. For Dedicated we can provide more granular deployment records.
[07:32] Lina Park: Do you have SOC 2 subservice orgs or vendor management? We use a third-party vector database vendor, we need to know how Redwood manages downstream vendors for in-scope services.
[07:43] Maya Chen: We maintain a vendor inventory and vendor risk program. For major subservice providers we provide attestations and evidence; we'll add the vendor list to the Trust Center view.
[07:56] Carlos Mendes: Is there a place to do a tabletop or runbook review with your team?
[08:01] Oliver Bates: Yes, we can run a tabletop for incident response and key compromise scenarios. That would be part of the follow-up ops session where we do the KMS envelope deep dive.
[08:12] Priya Rao: Ok let's talk timelines — we plan to be under audit in Q1 2027, want to finish procurement and tech eval by end of this year. Is that feasible?
[08:21] Maya Chen: Feasible, yes. If we get the list of in-scope systems and residency requirements this week, we can assemble a tailored control package and the legal team can start the DPA.
[08:33] Carlos Mendes: Any known limitations on API logs for certain operations? We sometimes need per-token logging for debug, which may be PII sensitive.
[08:42] Oliver Bates: We do not log full request payloads by default. We have redaction settings and token-level telemetry but not the plaintext unless explicitly enabled for debugging and with clear retention. For PII we recommend redaction before sending or Private deployment.
[08:59] Priya Rao: Great. What about exportability of logs for eDiscovery?
[09:04] Maya Chen: Exports are possible; we'll run through retention and export formats in the Trust Center docs.
[09:12] Lina Park: One last thing — can you confirm SLA around key rotation and notification windows?
[09:18] Oliver Bates: For CMKs in your account, you control rotation. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate with notices; we can add rotation windows and notification details to the runbook.
[09:29] Maya Chen: Okay summarizing — we'll send SOC 2 materials, grant read-only Trust Center access, and Oliver will prepare KMS runbook and example terraform snippets. Follow-up ops session week of 11/9 to deep-dive. Priya, Carlos, Lina any final asks?
[09:46] Priya Rao: No, just that we get the evidence by 11/5 so our audit prep can move.
[09:51] Carlos Mendes: No, sounds good.
[09:53] Lina Park: Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the KMS ops session and upload the docs. Linking the shared Trust Center here: https://redwood.example.com/trust/auriga-rls (placeholder link).
[10:12] Oliver Bates: I'll attach the rough envelope diagram to the follow-up invite.
[10:18] Maya Chen: Great. End of call.
